ddx.step1_summary:
- Chief complaint: Acute chest tightness for ~3 hours
- Symptoms: Mild shortness of breath (not at rest), wheeze, non-productive cough; recent URI last week (sore throat, runny nose) with lingering cough; cough slightly worse at night; chest feels tight rather than painful; exertion (stairs) increases dyspnea
- Onset/duration/severity: Chest tightness began ~3 hours prior to call; overall mild-to-moderate dyspnea, able to speak and not SOB at rest
- Aggravating/alleviating factors: Worse with exertion; has not used inhalers for ~1 week due to running out
- Past medical history: Asthma since childhood; severe exacerbation requiring intubation at ~16–17 years; allergic rhinitis/hay fever; childhood eczema; milk protein allergy (childhood)
- Medications/allergies: Previously on salbutamol (Ventolin) PRN and beclomethasone (Clenil Modulite) maintenance; ran out ~1 week ago; no known drug allergies
- Family history: Mother with eczema; father with asthma (atopic family history)
- Social history: University student; no tobacco/alcohol/drug history documented; known dust allergy
- Vital signs/exam: None recorded (telehealth); no peak flow available; patient not short of breath at rest; no chest pain reported
- Labs/imaging: None mentioned

V: Pulmonary embolism: Acute onset chest tightness and dyspnea over hours could represent PE, though risk factors and classic features are not elicited.
Coronary vasospasm (Prinzmetal) or atypical ischemia: Chest tightness can reflect cardiac ischemia, but age and associated wheeze make this less likely.
I: Viral upper respiratory infection with post-viral bronchial hyperreactivity/acute bronchitis: Recent cold with lingering cough; wheeze can occur post-viral and trigger asthma.
Community-acquired pneumonia: Post-URI cough with dyspnea; less likely without fever, sputum, or pleuritic pain.
I2: Loss of asthma control due to lack of controller medication (ICS) and reliever (SABA) for ~1 week: Medication lapse likely precipitated current symptoms.
A: Allergic asthma exacerbation: History of atopy (hay fever, eczema) and dust allergy; wheeze, chest tightness, and cough consistent with allergic/atopic asthma flare.
T: Spontaneous pneumothorax: Acute dyspnea and chest tightness could reflect PTX, though typical pleuritic pain and significant rest dyspnea are absent.

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Acute asthma exacerbation (likely viral-triggered and worsened by lapse in controller/reliever use)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Known asthma with atopic background, recent URI, current wheeze and chest tightness, and a week without ICS/SABA strongly support an asthma flare.
supporting_evidence: History of asthma with prior severe exacerbation requiring intubation
Ran out of both salbutamol and beclomethasone for ~1 week
Current wheeze, chest tightness, mild exertional dyspnea; no rest dyspnea
opposing_evidence: No objective measurements (peak flow, O2 sat) available to quantify severity
Lack of audible wheeze/exam findings due to telehealth limits certainty

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Post-viral bronchial hyperreactivity/acute viral bronchitis contributing to symptoms
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Recent cold with persistent non-productive cough can cause transient airway hyperreactivity and wheeze, often overlapping with asthma.
supporting_evidence: Recent sore throat/runny nose last week with ongoing cough
opposing_evidence: Presence of established asthma and medication lapse more directly explains wheeze and chest tightness
No fever or systemic symptoms suggesting more than mild viral illness

opposing_evidence: No fever, chills, pleuritic chest pain, or productive sputum reported
Not short of breath at rest; overall mild symptoms
